program_name: Business & Management (official English name on UNITO sources: 'Business & Management'; the programme microsite is titled 'Bachelor Program in Business and Management')
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). It is a stand-alone Italian first-cycle degree (laurea triennale) of the Department of Management 'Valter Cantino' / School of Management and Economics (SME), delivered 100% in English - not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree, and not an interuniversity/joint degree. UNITO 'Key information' consistently records 'Language: English' for every academic year of matriculation. The admission test (SAT Suite, College Board) is itself sat in English.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. Department of Management 'Valter Cantino' / School of Management and Economics (SME). UNITO 'Key information' records 'Teaching seat: Turin'; Apply@UniTo records 'Study location: Italy, Turin'.
degree_class: L-18 - Class of first degrees in Economic and Business Management Science (Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale). Listed on en.unito.it as 'Business & Management (L-18R)' under the reformed (DM 1649/2023) classes. UNITO internal course codes: 1106L31 (older cohorts, D.M. 270) and 1106L32 (current en.unito.it programme page id). Apply@UniTo course id: 564; a.y. 2026/27 intake id: 53.
admission_type: Restricted access - 'course with a local restricted number of places' (local numerus clausus). Selection is NOT by a UNITO-run written exam: candidates must sit the SAT Suite (College Board) and then register for one of the two UNITO admission calls (admission procedures), which produce a ranking list based purely on the SAT Suite score. No further UNITO test or interview is administered. Apply@UniTo states: 'This is a course with a fixed quota of places, which requires candidates to pass an admission test (SAT) before enrolment.' [uncertain - for a.y. 2025/2026 UNITO also accepted an ENGLISH TOLC-E taken between 2 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 as an alternative to the SAT; for a.y. 2026/2027 all consulted sources mention only the SAT, so the TOLC-E alternative appears to have been discontinued, but this could not be confirmed on the live programme page]
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027. (a) Candidates with an Italian qualification (Italians, EU and equivalents, non-EU legally resident in Italy) do NOT use Apply@UniTo: they pre-enrol on MyUniTO for one of the two admission procedures. First admission procedure: SAT Suite must have been taken between 1 January 2025 and 6 June 2026; if 'Admitted', enrolment 21 July 2026 (9:30) - 23 July 2026 (15:00). Second admission procedure (remaining places only): SAT Suite must have been taken between 1 January 2025 and 12 September 2026. (b) Candidates with a FOREIGN qualification who are EU/equivalent or non-EU legally residing in Italy apply on Apply@UniTo either in the 2nd admission call, 19 February - 15 April 2026, or in the 3rd/'fourth' admission call reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy for restricted-number programmes, 1 July - 14 September 2026 (23:59:59 CET, as displayed on the Apply@UniTo course page for intake 2026/27). [uncertain - the exact MyUniTO pre-enrolment opening/closing dates for the two 2026/27 admission procedures (2025/26 equivalents were 3-17 June 2025 and 1 July - 8 September 2025) could not be read on the live programme page, which was unreachable]
application_deadline_non_eu: A.y. 2026/2027. Non-EU candidates residing abroad (visa applicants, category 989, and Marco Polo category 988) must submit their Apply@UniTo application in the second admission call for undergraduate degree programmes: 19 February 2026 - 15 April 2026. The later calls (1 July - 14 September 2026 and 25 August - 19 October 2026) are explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy' and are therefore closed to non-EU applicants residing abroad. In addition, non-EU students requiring a visa must submit the pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform by 15 July 2026. Application fee on Apply@UniTo: EUR 60 (one-time, non-refundable, covers up to two programmes).
entry_exam_or_test: SAT Suite, administered by the College Board (satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat). UNITO does not run its own written test or interview: 'These competitions do not require students to take additional selection tests; instead, the admission process consists of ranking candidates based on their SAT Suite score.' Key mechanics: candidates must send the Official SAT Score Report digitally to UNITO using College Board code 9136 - University of Turin; the SAT may be taken more than once but only the MOST RECENT score counts (even if lower than a previous one); the SAT may be sat before obtaining the secondary school diploma. Validity window for a.y. 2026/2027: SAT taken between 1 January 2025 and 6 June 2026 (first admission procedure) or between 1 January 2025 and 12 September 2026 (second admission procedure). No minimum score is required in the second procedure. Additional Educational Requirements (OFA): candidates admitted with an SAT Suite 'Math' section score below 400 points must complete a compulsory-attendance supplementary Mathematics course plus an assessment test, which is a prerequisite for sitting first-year exams. [uncertain - the programme's own OFA page (snapshot 21 April 2026) still describes the OFA threshold in TOLC-E terms ('overall score of less than 12 points along with a score of less than 4 points in the Mathematics section'), which conflicts with the SAT Math < 400 rule stated on the admission-requirements page; the live pages could not be opened to resolve which wording is current] [uncertain - for a.y. 2025/2026 an ENGLISH TOLC-E obtained between 2 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 was also accepted; no such alternative is documented for 2026/2027]
academic_requirements: 1) Upper secondary school diploma that (a) grants access to a university programme of the same level in the country where it was issued and (b) was obtained after at least 12 years of global schooling, with at least the last two years attended in that same foreign education system. Applicants with 10 or 11 years of schooling must supplement it (one/two years of university studies with all exams passed, or a post-secondary qualification, or a Foundation Programme). 2) If a mandatory national university-entrance examination exists in the applicant's country (e.g. Greece, China, Cyprus, Spain), the same exam is also required for admission in Italy. 3) A university degree cannot replace the upper secondary diploma (art. 6, D.M. 270/2004). 4) SAT Suite score is the sole ranking criterion; no GPA threshold and no minimum SAT score are published for the second admission procedure. 5) Places (quota). A.y. 2026/2027 (Apply@UniTo, intake 2026/27): 'This degree program has 40 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad and 10 places for students in the Marco Polo program.' A.y. 2025/2026 (programme page, most recent full published breakdown): Italians, EU, equivalents and non-EU legally residing in Italy (category 990) = 200 places; non-EU residing abroad (category 989) = 40 places; Chinese 'Marco Polo' candidates (category 988) = 10 places, i.e. 250 places in total. [uncertain - the category-990 figure for a.y. 2026/2027 (200 in 2025/26) could not be verified because the live admission-requirements page was unreachable] 6) In the first admission procedure all places are open to all candidates; the second procedure only redistributes places left unfilled after the first, and is open to candidates who already hold the diploma and who did not participate in / were not admitted in / did not enrol after the first procedure.
language_requirements: English is the language of instruction and of the admission test. Apply@UniTo lists 'Language requirements: English' for this programme but does NOT specify a CEFR level or a list of accepted certificates, and no separate English-language certificate (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge) is required by any of the official UNITO sources consulted: English proficiency is effectively evidenced by the SAT Suite, which is sat in English and which is the compulsory admission test. Italian is NOT required: the UNITO Italian B2 (CLIQ / CISIA ITA-L2) requirement applies only to non-EU visa applicants enrolling in ITALIAN-taught free-access undergraduate programmes, which is not the case here. Free Italian language courses are offered to enrolled students as a support service. [uncertain - an English certificate requirement or exemption rule may be stated in the full 'Admission Regulations for Bachelor's Degrees 2026/27' (Regolamento ammissione lauree triennali), which is published only as a PDF on the unreachable UNITO servers]
required_documents: For applicants with a FOREIGN qualification applying through Apply@UniTo (undergraduate degrees): (1) valid ID card (Italian/EU and equivalent) or valid passport (non-EU); (2) for non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, a residence permit valid for university enrolment (art. 39(5), Legislative Decree 286/1998); (3) upper secondary study qualification obtained after at least 12 years of global schooling (EQF level 4 / ISCED 3), with proof of authenticity; if not yet completed, an official certificate attesting enrolment in the final year, the curriculum attended and the qualification to be obtained, plus the official score report of the years/semesters attended so far; (4) transcript of records (required if there is any doubt about the number of years of schooling); (5) the mandatory national entrance examination result, with proof of authenticity, where such an exam exists in the applicant's country; (6) country-specific additional documents; (7) Declaration of Value or CIMEA statement of comparability (not mandatory in general, but may be requested by the International Students Office); (8) SAT Suite Official Score Report sent digitally to UNITO with College Board code 9136; (9) payment of the EUR 60 application fee within the call deadline. Language rules: documents are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish; documents in any other language must be accompanied by a certified translation. Documents without a signature, seal or stamp are not accepted, and incomplete applications are not considered. Non-EU visa applicants must additionally complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment application (one programme only, with the competent Italian embassy/consulate) by 15 July 2026. Applicants with an Italian qualification instead register on the UniTo portal with SPID credentials and pre-enrol via MyUniTO, using the same e-mail address as their College Board account.

uncertainty_notes:
1) ACCESS PROBLEM. Direct access to www.business-management.unito.it, en.unito.it and www.unito.it was impossible during this research: the unito.it origin servers returned connection refused / connection timeout from every fetch path tried (WebFetch, headless Chrome, CORS proxies), and en.unito.it additionally sits behind a Cloudflare challenge that never reached the origin. Only apply.unito.it (hosted externally on DreamApply) loaded live. The remaining unito.it content was reconstructed from (a) Wayback Machine snapshots - business-management.unito.it/admission_requirements.html of 18 March 2025 (a.y. 2025/2026 content), the programme homepage of 20 June 2026, the OFA page of 21 April 2026, key_information of 24 September 2023, en.unito.it SAT/TOLC page of 13 February 2026 and en.unito.it international-application and required-documents pages of 16 May 2026 - and (b) verbatim search-engine extracts from the live admission-requirements page. No 2026/2027 Wayback snapshot of the programme's admission-requirements page exists, so the 2026/27 figures below marked as unverified could not be read in full context.
2) TEACHING LANGUAGE is unambiguous: fully English-taught, single-university (not interuniversity), not a pathway/curriculum inside an Italian-named degree.
3) NUMBER OF PLACES. The 40 non-EU-abroad + 10 Marco Polo figures are confirmed for a.y. 2026/2027 on the live Apply@UniTo page. The 200 places for category 990 (Italians/EU/equivalents/non-EU resident in Italy) are the confirmed a.y. 2025/2026 figure only; the 2026/2027 figure is assumed unchanged but not verified.
4) MYUNITO PRE-ENROLMENT WINDOWS for a.y. 2026/2027 (the registration windows for the two admission procedures, as opposed to the SAT-validity cut-offs and the enrolment window) could not be confirmed. For a.y. 2025/2026 they were 3-17 June 2025 (first procedure) and 1 July - 8 September 2025 (second procedure); the 2026/27 equivalents are very likely early June 2026 and 1 July - mid-September 2026, consistent with the 6 June 2026 / 12 September 2026 SAT cut-offs and the 21-23 July 2026 enrolment window, but this is inference.
5) OFA THRESHOLD INCONSISTENCY. The admission-requirements page states the OFA trigger as an SAT Suite Math score below 400 points, while the programme's own OFA page (still live as of the 21 April 2026 snapshot) describes a TOLC-E-based threshold (overall < 12 points together with Mathematics < 4). One of the two pages is stale; the SAT-based rule is the one consistent with the SAT-only admission mechanism.
6) ENGLISH TOLC-E ALTERNATIVE. For a.y. 2025/2026 an English TOLC-E obtained between 2 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 was accepted as an alternative to the SAT. All 2026/2027 sources mention only the SAT; the alternative appears to have lapsed but this could not be positively confirmed on a live 2026/27 page.
7) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE. No official source consulted imposes an IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge requirement; Apply@UniTo only records the bare word 'English' under 'Language requirements'. It remains possible that the full 'Admission Regulations for Bachelor's Degrees 2026/27' PDF (published in the Albo Ufficiale and linked from the unreachable programme page) contains a language-certificate clause.
8) LIVE-PAGE CAVEAT. Search-engine extracts of the live admission-requirements page also carried the sentence 'The admission requirements for the 2026-2027 academic year are being finalized ... check the page frequently for updates', alongside the concrete 2026/2027 SAT windows and the 21-23 July 2026 enrolment dates. This may be a stale banner or may indicate that some 2026/27 details were still provisional at the time of indexing; the dates given here should be re-verified against the live page once unito.it is reachable.
9) FEES. The EUR 2,800/year regional tuition figure quoted by Apply@UniTo is the 2025-26 maximum (range EUR 156-2,800 by income), and an additional programme contribution of EUR 400-5,100/year applies to this specific degree; 2026-27 fee amounts are published separately on the UNITO fee page.
